facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: At 2026-09-30 gross debt was USD 1,289.044 million at balance-sheet carrying value and net debt USD 1,125.587 million, which is 1.12x reported trailing twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1,006.666 million. Cash interest paid over the same twelve months was USD 70.509 million, so EBITDA covers it 14.28x. Both ratios are low because FY2025 earnings were cut by USD 738.115 million of non-cash goodwill and trademark impairments on the HEYDUDE brand, which pushed reported FY2025 EBITDA down to USD 228.797 million and the FY2025 net leverage to 4.81x; before impairments it was 1.14x. The creditor reading is that leverage is low on any basis and that the FY2025 headline ratio reflects accounting charges, not debt service. A caution runs the other way. The trailing figure holds USD 64.071 million of tariff refunds credited to cost of sales in the third quarter of 2026, which the issuer calls non-recurring. Without it, and before impairments, trailing EBITDA is USD 945.896 million and net leverage 1.19x. That is still low, so the refund does not change the view. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 8, 15; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6

facts.label: Cash-flow quality and shareholder returns
facts.text: Operating cash flow for the nine months to 2026-09-30 was USD 561.189 million and capital expenditure USD 53.615 million, so free cash flow was USD 507.574 million. Over the same nine months the company spent USD 506.194 million on share repurchases, 0.9973 of free cash flow, and a further USD 17.338 million on repurchases for tax withholding. Because the buyback absorbs nearly all free cash flow, net debt did not fall: it was USD 1,100.531 million at FY2025 and USD 1,125.587 million at 2026-09-30, and revolver drawings rose from USD 62.0 million to USD 113.0 million. The remaining repurchase authorization is about USD 1.7 billion against trailing free cash flow of USD 753.993 million, so the policy could lift leverage if management chose to fund buybacks from the revolver. The constraints the filings describe are a leverage cap of 3.25 to 1.00 and a minimum interest cover of 3.00 to 1.00 in the credit agreement, plus repurchase limits that depend on leverage; the definitions are not supplied, so the room cannot be measured. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 813.719 million is above FY2025 operating cash flow of USD 710.431 million mainly because of changes in income taxes and accounts payable, which the issuer attributes to the timing of payments and refunds and to inventory purchases. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 16–17, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 118, 138; calculation C7

facts.label: Liquidity and maturities
facts.text: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 163.457 million and USD 886.4 million of undrawn revolving facility. A further USD 15.0 million Asia facility is counted by the issuer as available borrowing, but the filings do not call it committed, so it is left out of the undrawn figure. Of the cash, USD 88.9 million is held outside the United States. No debt falls due until the revolving facility matures in November 2027; the term loan falls due on 2029-02-17 and the 2029 notes on 2029-03-15, together USD 850.000 million or 64.7% of face value, followed by the 2031 notes of USD 350.000 million. Both note issues are already callable at a premium that declines to par: the 2029 notes since 2024-03-15 and the 2031 notes since 2026-08-15. The creditor implication is that the revolver, the only committed liquidity backstop, comes up for renewal about a year after the as-of date and the filings disclose no extension. The 2029 wall is concentrated in two instruments that fall due within a month of each other. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 86–88; calculation C4

facts.label: Claims outside the debt figure
facts.text: Four claims sit outside gross debt. Operating lease liabilities of USD 374.074 million (USD 90.820 million current and USD 283.254 million long-term) are on their own balance-sheet lines and are not added to debt. Long-term income taxes payable of USD 641.563 million are excluded as well; the annual report ties them to uncertain tax positions of USD 636.973 million at FY2025, and no payment schedule is given. Purchase commitments were USD 307.5 million at 2026-09-30. Legal claims are accrued at USD 0.6 million with no estimate of a range, against a securities class action and four derivative actions. The long-term tax liability is the largest of these: at about 57% of net debt it would be material if it fell due in cash together. The filings do not say when or whether that happens, so the creditor treatment is to carry it as a named non-debt claim, not to add it to leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 116, 134, 152–153; calculation C8

facts.label: Data quality and definitions
facts.text: Three points limit how far the figures can be pushed. Reported EBITDA is a derived measure (income from operations plus depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement) because the issuer states neither EBITDA nor adjusted EBITDA, so no adjusted ratios are shown. The issuer's statements and its releases present expenses differently: the releases fold impairment charges into selling, general and administrative expenses, and the statements here follow the quarterly and annual reports. The September 2025 balance sheet is not printed in the supplied documents, so the nine months of 2025 appear in the income and cash flow statements only. Action: obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report if a year-on-year comparison of leverage is needed. - A few statement cells state that no value was printed (lines printed as a dash, lines folded into other lines in the quarterly reports, and current borrowings after 2023), so those cells are left as gaps, not zero. This restricts line-level comparison across annual and interim columns only. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the ratios. - The amount of the revolving facility commitment at 2023-12-31 is not stated in the supplied pages, only the availability of USD 558.7 million, so undrawn capacity for that date rests on the stated availability. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the latest period.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the cash flow: the company holds USD 163.5 million of cash and USD 901.4 million of available borrowings, has paid no dividend and funds repurchases mainly from operating cash flow, and HEYDUDE has just returned to growth. If HEYDUDE keeps growing and the Crocs Brand holds its international momentum, the brand and impairment concerns would fade. The view would turn more adverse if repurchases were funded from the revolving facility beyond free cash flow, if a further impairment of the HEYDUDE trademark were recorded, if the tariff refunds proved a one-off boost that margins cannot repeat, or if the proxy statement showed a controlling holder with different interests from creditors. It would turn more favourable if the issuer disclosed a leverage target and the credit agreements showed repurchase limits that bind well below current leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16–17, 22, 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

facts.text: No transaction or new debt issue is stated in the supplied documents for 2026. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a strong reading is that policy, not capacity, limits leverage. About USD 1.7 billion of repurchase authorization remains, 2.25x trailing free cash flow and 1.92x the undrawn revolver, and long-term income taxes payable equal 57.0% of net debt with no payment schedule. A buyback programme that outruns free cash flow, or a tax cash call, could take leverage well above the current 1.12x without any weakness in operations. The view would weaken if repurchases were funded from the revolver beyond free cash flow, if HEYDUDE revenue turned down again or its trademark were impaired further, or if tariffs rose on Vietnamese output. It would strengthen if management stated a leverage ceiling, if the revolver were extended well before November 2027, and if the credit agreements showed repurchase limits that bind at moderate leverage. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17; calculation C7; calculation C8

Direct-to-consumer was 52.4% of nine-month 2026 revenue and wholesale 47.6%, production is outsourced to third-party manufacturers, and capital expenditure is light. The business model supports cash-flow visibility through brand recognition, a proprietary material and a growing direct channel, but it is discretionary and fashion-led, so revenue visibility is limited to the season and cash flow depends on consumer demand and wholesale partners' orders. Debt service capacity is high because earnings are many times interest; refinancing confidence depends on brand durability.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 6–14

facts.label: Ownership and financial policy
facts.text: Crocs is a listed company with one class of common stock, no disclosed sponsor and a small record holder count. Financial policy is to buy back shares, not to pay dividends: it has never paid a cash dividend and repurchased shares in each of the last three years and in 2026. The mechanism is that repurchases compete with debt repayment for free cash flow, so the implication is that leverage stays near current levels instead of falling. The legal capacity to distribute is set by credit agreements that were not supplied, so willingness is evidenced but capacity is not tested. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

facts.text: Revenue growth was 2.0% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 on a reported basis, led by international Crocs Brand sales and direct-to-consumer, while North America wholesale for the Crocs Brand fell 11.1%. Volume and price both moved: unit volume fell in the nine months while average selling price rose. Revenue falls, gross margin compresses as tariffs and discounting rise, and operating deleverage cuts EBITDA further. Free cash flow falls but stays positive because capital expenditure is small and purchase commitments are largely cancellable. If repurchases continue, the revolver is drawn and net debt rises from 1.12x EBITDA; a HEYDUDE impairment would cut equity without cash. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied Crocs filings and releases are enough to support the requested credit snapshot as of the third quarter of 2026, so the analyses can proceed on filed figures, but covenant headroom, security terms and ratings cannot be established from them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118

The filings say the company met its financial covenants but print no covenant ratio, and no credit agreement, indenture, rating or market quote was supplied. Annual and interim statements run from fiscal 2023 to the nine months of 2026, so a trailing twelve-month view can be built by subtraction. Three differences between the filings and releases are recorded in the gaps, and one of them cannot be resolved from the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 86; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

spans.text: # Financial foundation for Crocs, Inc. (crox-1334036), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Crocs, Inc. (issuer crox-1334036), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. This module extracts the issuer's annual and interim statements, debt and liquidity into one US dollar basis and calculates leverage and cover from them, using the source readiness output for the run.
## Sources

| EX99.1_2026-03-31_crox_croxq12026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the first quarter of 2026 | 2026-04-30 | 25b6a72e0f19457baeaf30e3950ea611ce0034f7b145a6973e96f9f4c9fc3f66 | Total borrowings at 2026-03-31 as the release states them. |

| EX99.1_2026-06-30_crox_croxq22026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-07-30 | 27707336b30a4f357d789bf37f64744d3c54ccfa7cb575931a8679f39fd36440 | Not used for figures; read for events after the balance-sheet date. |

| Source readiness (CP-0) handoff | Source readiness output for this run | not stated | 013aa26e0401a1ed8962b804f28847d20544431d635ed6c9499af9a16d72a392 | Source register, gaps and period scope. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Crocs is lightly levered: net debt was 1.12x trailing twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and EBITDA covered cash interest 14.28x, so creditors have wide cover on filed figures, but nearly all free cash flow goes to shareholder returns.

The issuer reports no EBITDA, so it is built from operating income plus depreciation and amortization. FY2025 is distorted by non-cash impairments: net leverage reads 4.81x as reported and 1.14x before impairments. The trailing figure also holds a one-off tariff refund, and without it net leverage would be 1.19x. The revolving facility, drawn USD 113.0 million, matures in November 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6, 15–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6
### Leverage and coverage

At 2026-09-30 gross debt was USD 1,289.044 million at balance-sheet carrying value and net debt USD 1,125.587 million, which is 1.12x reported trailing twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1,006.666 million. Cash interest paid over the same twelve months was USD 70.509 million, so EBITDA covers it 14.28x. Both ratios are low because FY2025 earnings were cut by USD 738.115 million of non-cash goodwill and trademark impairments on the HEYDUDE brand, which pushed reported FY2025 EBITDA down to USD 228.797 million and the FY2025 net leverage to 4.81x; before impairments it was 1.14x. The creditor reading is that leverage is low on any basis and that the FY2025 headline ratio reflects accounting charges, not debt service.

A caution runs the other way. The trailing figure holds USD 64.071 million of tariff refunds credited to cost of sales in the third quarter of 2026, which the issuer calls non-recurring. Without it, and before impairments, trailing EBITDA is USD 945.896 million and net leverage 1.19x. That is still low, so the refund does not change the view.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 8, 15; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6
### Cash-flow quality and shareholder returns

Operating cash flow for the nine months to 2026-09-30 was USD 561.189 million and capital expenditure USD 53.615 million, so free cash flow was USD 507.574 million. Over the same nine months the company spent USD 506.194 million on share repurchases, 0.9973 of free cash flow, and a further USD 17.338 million on repurchases for tax withholding. Because the buyback absorbs nearly all free cash flow, net debt did not fall: it was USD 1,100.531 million at FY2025 and USD 1,125.587 million at 2026-09-30, and revolver drawings rose from USD 62.0 million to USD 113.0 million.

The remaining repurchase authorization is about USD 1.7 billion against trailing free cash flow of USD 753.993 million, so the policy could lift leverage if management chose to fund buybacks from the revolver. The constraints the filings describe are a leverage cap of 3.25 to 1.00 and a minimum interest cover of 3.00 to 1.00 in the credit agreement, plus repurchase limits that depend on leverage; the definitions are not supplied, so the room cannot be measured. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 813.719 million is above FY2025 operating cash flow of USD 710.431 million mainly because of changes in income taxes and accounts payable, which the issuer attributes to the timing of payments and refunds and to inventory purchases.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 16–17, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 118, 138; calculation C7
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 163.457 million and USD 886.4 million of undrawn revolving facility. A further USD 15.0 million Asia facility is counted by the issuer as available borrowing, but the filings do not call it committed, so it is left out of the undrawn figure. Of the cash, USD 88.9 million is held outside the United States. No debt falls due until the revolving facility matures in November 2027; the term loan falls due on 2029-02-17 and the 2029 notes on 2029-03-15, together USD 850.000 million or 64.7% of face value, followed by the 2031 notes of USD 350.000 million. Both note issues are already callable at a premium that declines to par: the 2029 notes since 2024-03-15 and the 2031 notes since 2026-08-15.

The creditor implication is that the revolver, the only committed liquidity backstop, comes up for renewal about a year after the as-of date and the filings disclose no extension. The 2029 wall is concentrated in two instruments that fall due within a month of each other.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 86–88; calculation C4
### Claims outside the debt figure

Four claims sit outside gross debt. Operating lease liabilities of USD 374.074 million (USD 90.820 million current and USD 283.254 million long-term) are on their own balance-sheet lines and are not added to debt. Long-term income taxes payable of USD 641.563 million are excluded as well; the annual report ties them to uncertain tax positions of USD 636.973 million at FY2025, and no payment schedule is given. Purchase commitments were USD 307.5 million at 2026-09-30. Legal claims are accrued at USD 0.6 million with no estimate of a range, against a securities class action and four derivative actions.

The long-term tax liability is the largest of these: at about 57% of net debt it would be material if it fell due in cash together. The filings do not say when or whether that happens, so the creditor treatment is to carry it as a named non-debt claim, not to add it to leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 116, 134, 152–153; calculation C8
### Data quality and definitions

Three points limit how far the figures can be pushed. Reported EBITDA is a derived measure (income from operations plus depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement) because the issuer states neither EBITDA nor adjusted EBITDA, so no adjusted ratios are shown. The issuer's statements and its releases present expenses differently: the releases fold impairment charges into selling, general and administrative expenses, and the statements here follow the quarterly and annual reports. The September 2025 balance sheet is not printed in the supplied documents, so the nine months of 2025 appear in the income and cash flow statements only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4

## Gaps

- The issuer states neither EBITDA nor adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization, and no adjusted ratios, adjusted EBITDA row or EBITDA bridge can be stated. This restricts every leverage and cover figure to a derived basis. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the issuer's covenant EBITDA definition or an investor presentation that states an adjusted EBITDA.

- The filings state compliance with the financial covenants but print no covenant ratio, definition or headroom, so covenant capacity cannot be measured from these figures. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the compliance certificates or the credit agreements.

- No supplied source states whether the two senior notes are secured, so they are left out of the debt stack and out of secured and senior subtotals, and their security cell is not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the indentures.

- The September 2025 balance sheet is not printed in the supplied documents, so the nine months of 2025 are stated for income and cash flow only, and a trailing twelve-month ratio at 2025-09-30 cannot be built. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report if a year-on-year comparison of leverage is needed.

- A few statement cells state that no value was printed (lines printed as a dash, lines folded into other lines in the quarterly reports, and current borrowings after 2023), so those cells are left as gaps, not zero. This restricts line-level comparison across annual and interim columns only. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the ratios.

- The amount of the revolving facility commitment at 2023-12-31 is not stated in the supplied pages, only the availability of USD 558.7 million, so undrawn capacity for that date rests on the stated availability. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the latest period.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Crocs is a two-brand footwear company with no sponsor disclosed, so creditors depend on brand durability and on a financial policy that currently directs nearly all free cash flow to share repurchases while debt stays low.

The Crocs Brand supplies 84.0% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 92.5% of segment operating profit. HEYDUDE, 16.0% of revenue, is recovering but carries a USD 1.14 billion trademark whose fair value exceeded its carrying value by less than 10% at the last annual test. Governance evidence is incomplete because the proxy statement was not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 106–107; calculation C1; calculation C2
### Key findings

The business rests on one brand. The Crocs Brand earned 92.5% of segment operating profit and 84.0% of revenue in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and its international revenue grew 8.8% while North America fell 2.4%, so creditor cash flow depends on one brand's demand across regions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 20; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C1; calculation C2

HEYDUDE is a recovering asset with impairment risk. Its revenue fell 24.7% from FY2023 to FY2025, it returned to growth of 6.1% in the third quarter of 2026, and the trademark carried at USD 1.14 billion has a fair-value cushion of under 10%, after USD 737.0 million of impairments in 2025. A further charge would be non-cash but would cut earnings and equity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 11, 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 154; calculation C3; calculation C4

Sourcing and tariff exposure is concentrated and flatters recent margins. Vietnam produced 45% of Crocs Brand output in 2025, and the largest manufacturer alone produced 45%. Third-quarter gross margin rose 770 bp to 66.2%, of which 630 bp came from tariff refunds that the issuer calls non-recurring, and tariffs of 10% to 12.5% still apply to the main sourcing countries.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 26

Channel mix is moving to direct-to-consumer, which lifts the margin mix but adds fixed cost. Direct-to-consumer was 52.4% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 52.1% in FY2025 and 48.0% in FY2023, and higher direct-to-consumer costs of USD 29.4 million drove most of the 3.6% rise in selling, general and administrative expense.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 26; calculation C5

Ownership and control cannot be assessed from the supplied documents. The company has never paid a cash dividend, had 36 holders of record, and has spent USD 250.0 million on repurchases in the latest quarter with about USD 1.7 billion of authorization left; who holds the shares and who sits on the board are in a proxy statement that was not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 106–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

Litigation is real but unquantified. A securities class action and four derivative actions allege that statements about wholesaler inventory misled investors; the company has accrued USD 0.6 million and states no estimate of the possible loss.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21
No transaction or new debt issue is stated for 2026. The last financing event was the February 2024 refinancing of the term loan, and the last acquisition was HEYDUDE in 2022.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 86–87; 10-K_2024-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 128
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the cash flow: the company holds USD 163.5 million of cash and USD 901.4 million of available borrowings, has paid no dividend and funds repurchases mainly from operating cash flow, and HEYDUDE has just returned to growth. If HEYDUDE keeps growing and the Crocs Brand holds its international momentum, the brand and impairment concerns would fade.

The view would turn more adverse if repurchases were funded from the revolving facility beyond free cash flow, if a further impairment of the HEYDUDE trademark were recorded, if the tariff refunds proved a one-off boost that margins cannot repeat, or if the proxy statement showed a controlling holder with different interests from creditors. It would turn more favourable if the issuer disclosed a leverage target and the credit agreements showed repurchase limits that bind well below current leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16–17, 22, 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so beneficial ownership, board independence and any controlling holder are not established, and the conclusion that no sponsor is disclosed rests on silence in the annual report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 106–107

- The credit agreements and indentures were not supplied, so the share repurchase capacity under the debt documents cannot be tested and the willingness-to-distribute reading is limited to what management did.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 85–88

- The third-quarter release mentions a business model change in the Crocs Brand North America direct-to-consumer channel with an approximate 2.7% effect on that channel's revenue but does not describe it, so the durability of North America revenue is not established.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 13
- Customer identities are not disclosed beyond the statement that no customer reached 10% of revenue, so wholesale concentration below that level cannot be judged.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 155

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No transaction or new debt issue is stated in the supplied documents for 2026. The most recent financing event was the February 2024 refinancing of the term loan: a new USD 820.0 million tranche refinanced the then-outstanding balance, repriced the margin and set the maturity at 2029-02-17, and USD 500.0 million remained outstanding at 2026-09-30. The senior notes date from 2021, when USD 350.0 million of 4.250% notes due 2029 and USD 350.0 million of 4.125% notes due 2031 were sold. The acquisition of HEYDUDE closed on 2022-02-17 for an aggregate preliminary purchase price of USD 2.3 billion, paid as USD 2.05 billion in cash and shares of Crocs common stock, financed by a USD 2.0 billion term loan and USD 50.0 million of revolver borrowings.

Since then the company has repaid debt: face value of borrowings fell from USD 1,710.0 million at year-end 2023 to USD 1,313.0 million at 2026-09-30, while the revolving facility rose from USD 62.0 million at year-end 2025 to USD 113.0 million. The creditor reading is that leverage has been reduced while shareholders were paid through repurchases, not through new debt-funded transactions.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Crocs has a strong fundamental credit profile because leverage is low and cash generation is high, but dependence on one brand, concentrated sourcing and a repurchase policy that absorbs nearly all free cash flow mean creditors rely on management not levering up.

Net debt was 1.12x trailing twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 and EBITDA covered cash interest 14.28x, with USD 886.4 million of undrawn revolver and no maturity before November 2027. The primary downside path is weaker demand at HEYDUDE or in the Crocs Brand together with tariff costs while repurchases continue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2
### Key findings

Leverage and cover are the main support. Net debt was 1.12x and EBITDA covered cash interest 14.28x on a trailing basis; the FY2025 reading of 4.81x is an artefact of non-cash impairments, since before impairments it was 1.14x, and without the tariff refund the trailing figure is 1.19x, so the low leverage does not depend on one-off items.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Cash generation is high but fully distributed. Repurchases took 99.7% of nine-month free cash flow, and the revolver rose while net debt did not fall, so debt service is secure today but deleveraging is a policy choice that management is not making.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 15

Business risk is concentrated. The Crocs Brand supplies 84.0% of revenue and 92.5% of segment operating profit, Vietnam makes 45% of its output, and tariffs of 10% to 12.5% apply to the main sourcing countries, so one brand, one sourcing region and one trade policy drive cash flow.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 22

HEYDUDE is the weakest asset. Its trademark has a fair-value cushion of under 10% after USD 737.0 million of impairments in 2025, so a further charge is plausible if its recovery stalls; the charge would be non-cash but would cut equity and reported earnings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 10

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing hinges on the revolver. Undrawn revolver of USD 886.4 million and cash of USD 163.5 million cover all needs until the revolver matures in November 2027, after which 64.7% of face value falls due in 2029, so the first test of market access is the revolver renewal.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 31
The margin outlook is flattered. The third-quarter gross margin rose 770 bp, of which 630 bp came from tariff refunds the issuer calls non-recurring, so the run rate is below the headline.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26

Governance and control are not established. The proxy statement was not supplied, so ownership, board independence and related-party items remain open, and the financial-policy reading rests on what management has done.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 106–107
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a strong reading is that policy, not capacity, limits leverage. About USD 1.7 billion of repurchase authorization remains, 2.25x trailing free cash flow and 1.92x the undrawn revolver, and long-term income taxes payable equal 57.0% of net debt with no payment schedule. A buyback programme that outruns free cash flow, or a tax cash call, could take leverage well above the current 1.12x without any weakness in operations.

The view would weaken if repurchases were funded from the revolver beyond free cash flow, if HEYDUDE revenue turned down again or its trademark were impaired further, or if tariffs rose on Vietnamese output. It would strengthen if management stated a leverage ceiling, if the revolver were extended well before November 2027, and if the credit agreements showed repurchase limits that bind at moderate leverage.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17; calculation C7; calculation C8
### Limitations

- No covenant ratio, definition or headroom is printed, so the finding that leverage is low rests on carrying-value ratios and cannot be tested against the leverage cap of 3.25x or the interest cover floor of 3.00x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 16
- The issuer states no EBITDA, so every leverage and cover figure uses an analyst-built measure; a covenant definition could move the level of the ratios although their direction would stand.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
- No rating, market quote or peer set was supplied, so the profile is not compared with typical high-yield issuers and nothing says how the market prices it.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The outlook rests on management's raised guidance of about 3% revenue growth for 2026, which has no independent check, so the recovery of HEYDUDE and the margin trend are less certain than the guidance implies.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Strengths and weaknesses

A strength is low leverage and wide cover. Net debt of USD 1,125.587 million against trailing reported EBITDA of USD 1,006.666 million gives 1.12x, and cash interest of USD 70.509 million is covered 14.28x, so earnings can fall substantially before debt service is strained. The credit implication is high resilience to an operating shock.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

A strength is cash generation with light capital needs. Trailing free cash flow of USD 753.993 million is 74.9% of trailing EBITDA, capital expenditure is 1.46% of revenue and purchase commitments are largely cancellable, so cash preservation levers exist in a downturn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

A strength is liquidity and a clear maturity path. Cash of USD 163.457 million and undrawn revolver of USD 886.4 million face no maturity until November 2027, and both note issues are callable at declining premiums, so refinancing is optional until the revolver renewal.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 88

A strength is a diversified route to market. Direct-to-consumer is above half of revenue, no customer reaches 10% of revenue and sales reach more than 85 countries, so wholesale partner loss is less damaging than for a wholesale-only footwear company.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 155

A strength is reduced debt since 2023. Face value of borrowings fell from USD 1,710.0 million at year-end 2023 to USD 1,313.0 million, and the term loan was refinanced to 2029 at lower margins, so refinancing risk was pushed out.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 15

A weakness is that distributions absorb free cash flow. Repurchases of USD 506.194 million equal 99.7% of nine-month free cash flow of USD 507.574 million, so net debt rose to USD 1,125.587 million from USD 1,100.531 million at year-end 2025, and the revolver rose by USD 51.0 million. The credit implication is that deleveraging depends on a policy change.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

A weakness is that one brand carries the credit. The Crocs Brand supplies 84.0% of revenue and 92.5% of segment operating profit, and its North America revenue fell 2.4% in nine months while international grew 8.8%, so regional momentum in one brand sets cash flow.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 12

A weakness is HEYDUDE valuation risk. The trademark of USD 1.14 billion has a cushion under 10% after USD 737.0 million of 2025 impairments; HEYDUDE grew 6.1% in the third quarter but is below its FY2023 revenue, so an impairment would cut equity of USD 1,345.007 million further.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 24

A weakness is concentrated sourcing and tariffs. Vietnam makes 45% of Crocs Brand output and one manufacturer 45%, tariffs of 10% to 12.5% remain, and USD 64.071 million of refunds reduced third-quarter cost of sales, so margins carry both a cost and a one-off flattering effect.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 26; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8

A weakness is that claims outside debt are large and unscheduled. Long-term income taxes payable of USD 641.563 million equal 57.0% of net debt, operating lease liabilities are USD 374.074 million and a securities class action is unquantified, so claims on cash exist beyond the debt shown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20–21

### Company description and operating model

Crocs designs and sells casual footwear and accessories through two brands, the Crocs Brand and HEYDUDE, in more than 85 countries. Direct-to-consumer was 52.4% of nine-month 2026 revenue and wholesale 47.6%, production is outsourced to third-party manufacturers, and capital expenditure is light. The business model supports cash-flow visibility through brand recognition, a proprietary material and a growing direct channel, but it is discretionary and fashion-led, so revenue visibility is limited to the season and cash flow depends on consumer demand and wholesale partners' orders. Debt service capacity is high because earnings are many times interest; refinancing confidence depends on brand durability.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 6–14
### Ownership and financial policy

Crocs is a listed company with one class of common stock, no disclosed sponsor and a small record holder count. Financial policy is to buy back shares, not to pay dividends: it has never paid a cash dividend and repurchased shares in each of the last three years and in 2026. The mechanism is that repurchases compete with debt repayment for free cash flow, so the implication is that leverage stays near current levels instead of falling. The legal capacity to distribute is set by credit agreements that were not supplied, so willingness is evidenced but capacity is not tested.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
### Revenue durability

Revenue growth was 2.0% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 on a reported basis, led by international Crocs Brand sales and direct-to-consumer, while North America wholesale for the Crocs Brand fell 11.1%. Volume and price both moved: unit volume fell in the nine months while average selling price rose. The mechanism is that price and mix support revenue while volume is soft, which makes revenue less durable than the headline; the implication is moderate revenue visibility with no contract or recurring element, and a fashion-cycle exposure at HEYDUDE, whose revenue fell from USD 949.393 million in FY2023 to USD 714.840 million in FY2025.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, page 154; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 12
### Margin resilience

Gross margin was 60.9% in the nine months against 59.5%, helped by tariff refunds, channel mix and lower product costs and offset by product mix and incremental duties. Selling, general and administrative expense rose 3.6%, driven by direct-to-consumer cost, so operating leverage is positive only while revenue grows. The mechanism is that rising rent and marketplace costs raise the fixed-cost share, and the implication is that margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but a demand shock would squeeze them; adjusted operating margin guidance of about 20.5% for the fourth quarter already points below the nine-month level.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10
### Cash conversion and capital intensity

Trailing free cash flow of USD 753.993 million is 74.9% of trailing reported EBITDA, with capital expenditure at 1.46% of revenue and cash interest of USD 70.509 million. Working capital absorbed cash in the nine months, as inventories rose to USD 413.030 million and receivables to USD 355.022 million, and the tax cash timing improved operating cash flow. The mechanism is that low capital intensity leaves most earnings as cash; the implication is that capital expenditure can be cut in a downturn but the cash is currently directed to repurchases, not to deleveraging.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 32
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense: competitors include larger footwear groups with greater resources and some wholesale partners compete with Crocs' own stores, so price pressure and wholesale terms could weaken margins. Buyer power sits with wholesale customers, but none reaches 10% of revenue and direct-to-consumer exceeds half of revenue, which limits it. Supplier power is moderate because manufacturing capability is broadly available, though Vietnam and one manufacturer are concentrated. The threat of substitutes and new entrants is relevant to a brand-driven category with low barriers in casual footwear. The credit implication is that competition shows up in margins and wholesale volume, not in sudden loss of access to supply.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 17, 155
### Macro and policy factors

Political and regulatory factors are material: tariffs of 10% to 12.5% apply to imports from countries that supply Crocs, the Supreme Court ruling on emergency tariffs led to refunds, and further trade actions remain uncertain. Economic factors are material because the issuer says consumers face elevated rates and inflation and wholesale partners act cautiously, and the Middle East conflict has cut revenue in some distributor markets. Social and technological categories do not change the credit view and are skipped.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 22
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are low leverage, wide interest cover, light capital needs, a direct channel above half of revenue and no maturity before November 2027. Weaknesses are one-brand dependence, HEYDUDE's valuation cushion, repurchases that absorb free cash flow and unscheduled tax and litigation claims. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a stated leverage ceiling, a refinanced revolver and continued HEYDUDE growth. Threats that could weaken it are tariffs on Vietnamese output, a consumer slowdown and debt-funded buybacks.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile

- Scale and market position: Strong. Revenue of USD 4,101.148 million on a trailing basis, 500 Crocs Brand and 78 HEYDUDE stores and sales in more than 85 countries absorb shocks, although market share is not stated.
- Competitive advantage: Average. The clog and a proprietary material are distinctive, but fashion cycles and HEYDUDE's decline limit durability.
- Business diversification: Average. Two brands and two channels, but one brand carries most profit and sourcing is concentrated.
- Cost and capex flexibility: Strong. Capital expenditure is a small share of revenue and purchase commitments are largely cancellable.
- Margin stability: Average. Gross margin has ranged from 55.8% in FY2023 to 60.9% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and now includes refunds and tariffs, while direct-to-consumer costs rise.
- Free cash flow stability: Strong. Free cash flow was positive and large in every period shown, with working capital swings.
- Ability to refinance and access capital markets: Average. The term loan was refinanced in 2024 and both notes are callable, but there is no rating and the revolver renews in November 2027.
- Liquidity position: Strong. Cash of USD 163.457 million and undrawn revolver of USD 886.4 million cover all near-term needs.
- Financial policy and governance: Average. No dividend and debt reduced since 2023, but repurchases absorb free cash flow and ownership and board evidence is incomplete.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 15–16, 30
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months, management guides 2026 revenue growth of about 3%, with the Crocs Brand up about 4% and HEYDUDE about flat, and fourth-quarter revenue up 7% to 9%; these support margin and cash flow if delivered, but they are management's expectations. Tailwinds are international Crocs Brand growth, HEYDUDE's return to growth and tariff refunds, of which about USD 67 million was received against an estimated USD 75 million to USD 80 million in total. Headwinds are tariffs, cautious wholesale partners, direct-to-consumer costs and the end of one-off refunds. Over three to five years the key factor is whether HEYDUDE stabilises and whether policy keeps leverage low; the filings give no medium-term targets.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_crox_croxq32026-pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, page 22
### Downside scenario

The downside begins with a consumer slowdown or a tariff increase on Vietnamese output that cuts Crocs Brand demand and wholesale orders while direct-to-consumer costs stay fixed. Revenue falls, gross margin compresses as tariffs and discounting rise, and operating deleverage cuts EBITDA further. Free cash flow falls but stays positive because capital expenditure is small and purchase commitments are largely cancellable. If repurchases continue, the revolver is drawn and net debt rises from 1.12x EBITDA; a HEYDUDE impairment would cut equity without cash. Management levers are to suspend repurchases and to cut capital expenditure, either of which restores liquidity; resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because undrawn revolver of USD 886.4 million exceeds a year of cash interest by a wide margin. A first observable break would be negative Crocs Brand growth in two consecutive quarters or a rising revolver balance beside falling free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_crox.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 22
### Overall credit view

Overall, Crocs presents an adequate business profile supported by global brand scale, a growing direct channel and low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on one brand, concentrated sourcing and a repurchase policy that absorbs nearly all free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears strong because trailing free cash flow of USD 753.993 million is 74.9% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on renewal of the revolver due November 2027 and on market access for the 64.7% of face value due in 2029. The primary downside path is a demand or tariff shock at the Crocs Brand while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the proxy statement, a covenant EBITDA definition and a rating or market quotes. Top Risk: a debt-funded repurchase programme meeting a tariff or HEYDUDE setback.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C7
